verdict.rationale: Gitleaks handles many items in one invocation: the `dir` command scans whole directories of files, the `git` command scans a repo's full patch history via `git log -p`, and gitleaks.io claims scans across all of a team's pull requests and commits. This is batch scanning only, not general bulk operations; there is no documented multi-repo/org-wide batch command and no bulk triage or remediation of findings. missing for 10: documented multi-repository or org-wide bulk scanning, bulk actions on findings (e.g., resolve or ignore many at once), API or agent-oriented batch interface, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can perform bulk operations across many items at once

citations.quote: The `dir` (aliases include `files`, `directory`) command lets you scan directories and files.
Under the hood, gitleaks uses the `git log -p` command to scan patches.
You can use it to automatically run a gitleaks scan on all your team's pull requests and commits, or run on-demand scans.
